lesson.title: React useEffect: Dependencies, Event Listeners and Cleanup
lesson.goal: learn the React useEffect hook: run side effects on mount and on state changes, and clean them up

sources.title: React useEffect: Dependencies, Event Listeners and Cleanup

steps.title: Create counter component with useState
steps.instructions:
Scaffold with `npm create vite@latest my-app -- --template react`, run `cd my-app && npm install`, then create `src/MyComponent.jsx` with `useState(0)` count state, a `

Count: {count}

` and an Add button calling `addCount`. Render `` from `App.jsx` and start it with `npm run dev`.

targets.caption: Count state starting at zero
Handler that increments count
Rendered counter paragraph

explanations.topic: Importing useState and useEffect from React
Declaring a count state variable and setter
Updater function using previous state

hints: Import both hooks: import React, { useState, useEffect } from 'react'.

Declare const [count, setCount] = useState(0) inside the component and show {count} in a

.
Write function addCount() { setCount(c => c + 1); } and pass it as onClick={addCount} (no parentheses).
Import MyComponent in App.jsx, render <MyComponent />, then run npm run dev and open the Local URL.
common_mistakes: Writing onClick={addCount()} which calls the function during render instead of on click.
Forgetting to export default MyComponent or to render it in App.jsx.
Calling useState outside the component function.
Running npm run dev before cd my-app && npm install.

steps.title: Run effect on every render
steps.instructions: Inside MyComponent call `useEffect(() => { document.title = `Count: ${count}`; });` with no second argument. Click Add and watch the tab title update on every render.

targets.caption: Effect with no dependency array runs after every render
Side effect: update the browser tab title with count

explanations.topic: useEffect runs side code every time the component re-renders
useEffect takes two arguments: a function and an array of dependencies
Omitting the dependency array makes the effect run after every render
The effect also runs initially when the component mounts

hints: Call useEffect near the top of your component, after your useState line.
Pass useEffect a single arrow function and leave out the second argument (the dependency array).
Inside the arrow function, assign a template string that includes your count variable to document.title.
Don't forget to add useEffect to your import from 'react', alongside useState.
common_mistakes: Forgetting to import useEffect from 'react' (ReferenceError: useEffect is not defined).
Adding an empty dependency array [], which makes the effect run only on mount, so the title won't update on clicks.
Using regular quotes instead of backticks, so ${count} appears literally in the title.
Writing document.title = ... directly in the component body instead of inside the function passed to useEffect.
Calling useEffect inside a condition or inside the click handler instead of at the top level of the component.

steps.title: Run effect only on mount
steps.instructions: In src/MyComponent.jsx pass an empty dependency array as useEffect's second argument, useEffect(() => {...}, []), and confirm the title is set only once on mount. Then revert to the Count: ${count} title.

targets.caption: Add [] as the second argument so it runs only on mount
Press Add: the tab title should not change after the first render

explanations.topic: An empty dependency array runs the effect only on mount
The title updates once and not after later re-renders
One-and-done effects like setting a static title
Why skipping unnecessary re-runs matters

hints: useEffect takes a second argument after the callback function.
Pass an empty array of dependencies to run the effect only when the component mounts.
Close the arrow function's braces, then add a comma and [] before the closing parenthesis: useEffect(() => { ... }, []);
Reload the page and press Add. The title should show the initial value and then stay the same.
common_mistakes: Putting [] inside the arrow function body instead of passing it as the second argument to useEffect.
Leaving out the dependency array entirely, which makes the effect run after every render.
Expecting the title to update after pressing Add. With [] it only updates once, on mount.
Forgetting to import useEffect from 'react'.

steps.title: Depend on count, add subtract
steps.instructions: Change the dependency array to [count] so the effect runs on mount and whenever count changes. Add a Subtract button calling a subtractCount function that does setCount(c => c - 1).

targets.caption: Effect now depends on count
New function that decrements count
New Subtract button on the page

explanations.topic: Putting a value in the dependency array runs the effect on mount and when that value changes
No dependency array means the effect runs on every re-render, even unrelated ones
Effect fires whenever count changes, whether it goes up or down

hints: The second argument to useEffect is the dependency array. What should go inside it so the effect reruns when count changes?
Write it as `}, [count]);` at the end of your useEffect call.
Copy your addCount function, rename it subtractCount, and change + 1 to - 1: `setCount(c => c - 1)`.
Add `<button onClick={subtractCount}>Subtract</button>` next to the Add button. Clicking either one should update the tab title.
common_mistakes: Leaving the array empty `[]`, so the title only updates once on mount.
Writing `onClick={subtractCount()}`, which calls the function during render and causes an infinite re-render loop.
Writing `setCount(count - 1)` when the updater form `c => c - 1` is what's expected.
Forgetting to rename the copied function, so both buttons still add.

steps.title: Add color state as dependency
steps.instructions: Add color state with useState('green'), a Change color button calling changeColor that toggles green/red, style the count paragraph with style={{color: color}}, and set the title to Count: ${count} ${color}. Use [count, color] as dependencies so the title updates when either changes.

targets.caption: New color state starts as green
Toggles color using the previous state
Effect re-runs when count or color changes
Click it and watch the tab title update

explanations.topic: Updater function with previous state and ternary toggle
Inline style needs a JS object, hence double curly braces
Missing dependency: color changes but title does not update
Effect runs whenever any value in the dependency array changes

hints: Add a second state variable for color next to count, starting as 'green'.
Write a changeColor function that calls setColor with an updater: c => c === 'green' ? 'red' : 'green'.
Style the count paragraph with style={{color: color}}, which is an object inside JSX braces.
Include color in the title template and add color to the dependency array: [count, color].
common_mistakes: Leaving color out of the dependency array. The paragraph changes color but the document title stays stale.
Writing style={color} or style="color" instead of a double-braced object style={{color: color}}.
Writing onClick={changeColor()}, which calls the function during render instead of passing it.
Using = instead of === in the ternary, which assigns the value instead of comparing it.
Forgetting backticks for the template literal in document.title.

steps.title: Track window size with listener
steps.instructions: In src/MyComponent.jsx add `width`/`height` state from `window.innerWidth`/`window.innerHeight`, render them as `Window width: {width}px` and `Window height: {height}px`, and write `handleResize` updating both. Temporarily call `window.addEventListener('resize', handleResize)` and a console.log directly in the component body, then resize and watch the console flood.

targets.caption: Width state initialized from the window
Resize handler updating width and height
Listener added directly in the component body (the problem)
Rendered window dimensions

explanations.topic: Displayed size doesn't update without a resize listener
Adding a resize event listener with a callback
Every re-render adds another listener, flooding the console

hints: You need two state variables, each initialized from a property of the window object.
Write a handleResize function that sets both state variables from window.innerWidth and window.innerHeight.
Call window.addEventListener('resize', handleResize) in the component body, plus a console.log so you can watch it run.
Open DevTools Console and drag the window edge: the log count should climb with every render.
common_mistakes: Calling handleResize() when passing it (addEventListener('resize', handleResize())) instead of passing the function reference.
Typo 'setheight' with lowercase h so the setter is undefined.
Using window.width/window.outerWidth instead of window.innerWidth.
Forgetting 'px' or the curly braces around {width} in the JSX.
Thinking the flood of 'EVENT LISTENER ADDED' logs is your bug; it is the intended demonstration, fixed in the next step with useEffect.

steps.title: Add listener inside useEffect once
steps.instructions: In src/MyComponent.jsx, move the window.addEventListener('resize', handleResize) call and its log into useEffect(() => {...}, []) so the listener is added only on mount. Resize the window and check that the console shows the listener added only once (twice in StrictMode dev).

targets.caption: Wrap the addEventListener call and its log in useEffect
Empty dependency array: run only on mount

explanations.topic: Adding the event listener only once, when the component mounts
An empty dependency array means the effect runs on mount only
StrictMode runs effects twice in development (setup, cleanup, setup)

hints: The listener is currently added in the component body, so it runs on every render. Move it somewhere that runs once.
Put the addEventListener call and its console.log inside useEffect(() => { ... }).
Pass an empty array [] as the second argument to useEffect so it only runs on mount.
Resize the window and open DevTools. You should see the 'added' log once, or twice if StrictMode is on.
common_mistakes: Leaving the old addEventListener call in the component body as well, so listeners still pile up on every render.
Omitting the dependency array, which makes the effect run after every render.
Putting [] inside the arrow function instead of passing it as useEffect's second argument.
Thinking two logs is a bug: React StrictMode in development intentionally runs the effect setup twice.
Forgetting to import useEffect from 'react'.

steps.title: Return cleanup removing listener
steps.instructions: Inside that effect, return a cleanup function that calls window.removeEventListener('resize', handleResize) and logs that the listener was removed. Refresh the page and confirm the console shows the StrictMode add, remove, add sequence.

targets.caption: Cleanup function returned from useEffect removes the resize listener
StrictMode runs add, cleanup, then add again in development

explanations.topic: Returning a cleanup function from useEffect
Cleanup runs before the next re-render or on unmount
Why remove event listeners: avoid unexpected behavior and free resources
StrictMode add/remove/add sequence in the console

hints: Inside the same useEffect that adds the resize listener, add a return statement at the end.
The return value must be a function: return () => { ... }.
In that function call window.removeEventListener('resize', handleResize) with the same callback you passed to addEventListener.
Add console.log('EVENT LISTENER REMOVED'), refresh, and open DevTools > Console to see added, removed, added.
common_mistakes: Calling removeEventListener directly instead of returning a function that calls it.
Passing a new arrow function to removeEventListener instead of the same handleResize reference, so nothing is removed.
Putting the return in a different useEffect or outside the effect.
Thinking the removed/added log pair means a bug. It is React StrictMode's intentional double run in development.

steps.title: Add second useEffect for title
steps.instructions: Add a second useEffect that sets document.title to the current size, with [width, height] as its dependency array. Resize the window and watch the browser tab title update with the new size.

targets.caption: Second useEffect sets the document title from width and height
Browser tab title updates as the window is resized

explanations.topic: A component can have more than one useEffect hook
Dependency array [width, height] re-runs the effect when the size changes
Effect runs on mount, so the title shows the size immediately

hints: Add a separate useEffect call below the existing one rather than editing the listener effect.
Inside it, assign a template string to document.title using your width and height state.
Pass [width, height] as the second argument so it re-runs when either changes.
Full form: useEffect(() => { document.title = `Size: ${width} x ${height}`; }, [width, height]);
common_mistakes: Using regular quotes instead of backticks, so ${width} appears literally in the title
Leaving out the dependency array or passing [] so the title never updates after mount
Putting the title code inside the event-listener effect's cleanup return
Writing document.Title (wrong case) so nothing changes
